name: PSECT
short: Declare or resume a code or data section
description: Groups code or data into a named program section. PSECT selects where subsequent instructions, DB/DW data, or DS storage belong. The linker places relocatable sections in memory; absolute sections use fixed addresses. Repeating the same name resumes that section.

operands.name: name
operands.description: Section name, such as myCode. The name identifies the section; it is not a memory address.

operands.name: flag...
operands.description: Optional comma-separated attributes. When resuming an existing section, its name alone is sufficient.

flags.name: class=name
flags.description: Allowed memory range: CODE for instructions; CONST for constants; COMRAM for Access Bank variables; BANK1 for bank 1 variables.

flags.name: space=0 / space=1
flags.description: 0 = program memory (also EEPROM on PIC18); 1 = data memory. Banks share space=1 and are distinguished by their full addresses.

flags.name: delta=1
flags.description: One byte per address unit; use this default for PIC18. DW still emits two bytes per value.

flags.name: reloc=2
flags.description: Start at an even byte address, required for PIC18 executable code. More generally, reloc sets a power-of-two alignment; it does not fix an address.

flags.name: bit
flags.description: Allocate bit-sized objects. DS counts bits and labels hold bit addresses; divide a label by 8 for the byte address and use label & 7 for the bit number.

flags.name: abs
flags.description: Section base is zero and cannot be relocated by the linker. Combine with ovrld and ORG for a fixed location.

flags.name: ovrld
flags.description: Overlay contributions from different source modules instead of concatenating them. Combined with abs, labels have absolute addresses. It does not make overlapping executable contents safe.

flags.name: global / local
flags.description: global is the default: combine same-name sections across modules. local keeps each module's section separate; use a class to place it.

flags.name: size=max
flags.description: Maximum section size, checked after contributions from modules have been combined.

flags.name: limit=address
flags.description: Highest permitted address of the section; checked at link time (PIC18 only).

flags.name: lowdata
flags.description: Keep the whole section below address 0x1000; this is not an Access Bank selector.

flags.name: noexec
flags.description: Mark non-executable contents for debugging. It does not prevent the processor from executing those bytes.

flags.name: pure
flags.description: Declare contents read-only; actual enforcement depends on the target and linker.

flags.name: with=section
flags.description: Place this section in the same memory page as the named section.

flags.name: note
flags.description: Tool/debugger information that is excluded from the final program image.

flags.name: optim=names
flags.description: Colon-separated optimization permissions. Has no effect in standalone pic-as, which performs no optimizations.

flags.name: inline / keep / merge / split
flags.description: Deprecated optimization attributes; the guide uses optim instead. They are not needed for the examples below.

notes: A section name is an identifier, not a memory type or an address. Its attributes and linker class determine placement. A linker class names an allowed range of addresses.

Include <xc.inc> to use predefined sections and linker classes. In PIC18 assembly, the predefined data section holds constants in program memory; it does not create initialized variables in data memory.
DS reserves storage without initializing it. To give a variable an initial value, execute a store instruction, or copy an initial value from program memory.

Resuming a section keeps its attributes. Within one source file, new contents append to that section, even with ovrld. Global sections with the same name normally concatenate across object files; ovrld overlays their contributions instead.
global here concerns section merging; it does not export labels. Use the GLOBAL directive to make a label visible to other source modules.
PSECT itself is processed during assembly and has no processor opcode or execution cycle count.
example:
#include <xc.inc>

PSECT myCode,class=CODE,reloc=2
first_value:
    MOVLW 0x2A           ; first routine loads WREG with 0x2A
    RETURN

; Append another routine to the same section.
PSECT myCode
second_value:
    MOVLW 0x00           ; second routine loads WREG with 0
    RETURN
; The linker assigns myCode an even program-memory address.

rows.name: edata (EEDATA)
rows.description: Initial contents to program into the device's EEPROM (Electrically Erasable Programmable Read-Only Memory).

rows.name: udata (RAM)
rows.description: Uninitialized variables in general-purpose data memory.

rows.name: udata_acs (COMRAM)
rows.description: Uninitialized variables in the Access Bank's general-purpose memory.

rows.name: udata_bankn (BANKN)
rows.description: Uninitialized variables in bank n, for example udata_bank1. The bank must exist on the device.

examples.title: Program-memory constants
examples.code:
#include <xc.inc>

PSECT data
message:
    DB "OK",0             ; bytes: 4F 4B 00
values:
    DW 0x1234             ; bytes: 34 12 on PIC18
; These bytes are stored in program memory.
; Read them with TBLPTR, TBLRD and TABLAT.

examples.title: Access Bank variables
examples.code:
#include <xc.inc>

PSECT udata_acs
counter: DS 1             ; reserve one byte; no initial value

PSECT accessCode,class=CODE,reloc=2
init_counter:
    CLRF counter,0        ; execute to initialize counter to 0
    RETURN

examples.title: Variables in a specific bank
examples.code:
#include <xc.inc>

PSECT udata_bank1
myBuffer: DS 4            ; four bytes in bank 1

PSECT bankCode,class=CODE,reloc=2
store_first:
    BANKSEL myBuffer      ; select the bank containing myBuffer
    MOVLW 0x2A
    MOVWF BANKMASK(myBuffer),1 ; banked access: myBuffer[0] = 0x2A
    RETURN

examples.title: Bit variables
examples.code:
#include <xc.inc>

PSECT bitVars,class=COMRAM,space=1,bit
ready: DS 1               ; reserve one bit, not one byte

PSECT bitCode,class=CODE,reloc=2
clear_ready:
    BCF ready/8,ready&7,0 ; byte address = ready/8; bit = ready&7
    RETURN

examples.title: Fixed reset vector
examples.code:
#include <xc.inc>

PSECT resetVec,class=CODE,abs,ovrld,reloc=2
ORG 0x0000
    GOTO start            ; reset vector at program address 0

PSECT appCode,class=CODE,reloc=2
start:
    BRA start             ; linker places this code elsewhere
; In a relocatable section, ORG is an offset within the section.
; ORG alone does not give a relocatable section a fixed address.

examples.title: Place a relocatable section with the linker
examples.code:
#include <xc.inc>

PSECT placedCode,class=CODE,reloc=2
routine:
    RETURN
; At link time, pass this pic-as driver option:
;   -Wl,-PplacedCode=0x200
; This places the section at program address 0x200.
; Do not combine this placement option with an abs section.

name: DB
description: Emits one byte for each numeric value or character into the current program-memory section. A string emits its characters in order.

operands.name: value
operands.description: An 8-bit value, character, or string; separate multiple items with commas.

notes: On PIC18 with delta=1, bytes are consecutive with no padding between them. Strings have no automatic zero terminator; add ,0 when required.
DB does not allocate a variable in data memory. Use DS for storage there. Data bytes must not be reached as executable code.
example:
#include <xc.inc>

PSECT data
message:
    DB "OK",0             ; three bytes: 4F 4B 00

PSECT readBytes,class=CODE,reloc=2
read_message:
    MOVLW LOW(message)
    MOVWF TBLPTRL,0
    MOVLW HIGH(message)
    MOVWF TBLPTRH,0
    MOVLW LOW HIGHWORD(message)
    MOVWF TBLPTRU,0
    TBLRD*+               ; TABLAT = 0x4F (O); pointer advances
    TBLRD*+               ; TABLAT = 0x4B (K)
    TBLRD*                ; TABLAT = 0x00 (terminator)
    RETURN

name: DW
description: Emits two bytes for each numeric value or character into the current program-memory section. On PIC18 the low byte comes first.

operands.name: value
operands.description: A 16-bit value, character, or string; each string character occupies a separate 16-bit word.

notes: A PIC18 address unit is still one byte (delta=1); DW determines the width of each emitted value. No automatic string terminator is added.
DW does not reserve data-memory variables. This page documents pic-as; PIC18 behavior in older MPASM code differs.
example:
#include <xc.inc>

PSECT data
words:
    DW 0x1234,0xABCD      ; four bytes: 34 12 CD AB

PSECT readWords,class=CODE,reloc=2
read_first_word:
    MOVLW LOW(words)
    MOVWF TBLPTRL,0
    MOVLW HIGH(words)
    MOVWF TBLPTRH,0
    MOVLW LOW HIGHWORD(words)
    MOVWF TBLPTRU,0
    TBLRD*+               ; TABLAT = 0x34 (low byte)
    MOVFF TABLAT,PRODL
    TBLRD*+               ; TABLAT = 0x12 (high byte)
    MOVFF TABLAT,PRODH    ; PRODH:PRODL = 0x1234
    RETURN

name: DS
description: Reserves space in the current section without giving it an initial value. In an ordinary PIC18 data-memory section, count is the number of bytes; in a bit section, it is the number of bits.

operands.name: count
operands.description: Number of address units to reserve; use a data-memory section for variables.

notes: The label identifies the reserved storage. Initialize it by executing instructions; DS 1 does not store the number 1.
example:
#include <xc.inc>

PSECT udata_acs
counter: DS 1             ; one uninitialized byte
buffer:  DS 4             ; four uninitialized bytes

PSECT initVars,class=CODE,reloc=2
init_vars:
    CLRF counter,0        ; counter = 0 at runtime
    MOVLW 0x2A
    MOVWF buffer,0        ; first buffer byte = 0x2A
    RETURN

name: EQU
description: Gives a symbol a constant value that the assembler can use in expressions. It emits no data and reserves no storage.

operands.name: symbol
operands.description: New name placed before EQU, with no colon.

operands.name: expression
operands.description: Constant expression to associate with the symbol.

notes: The symbol must not already be defined in the same module. EQU cannot redefine a value; SET is available when redefinition is needed.
EQU creates an assembler symbol. #define replaces source text before assembly and can take arguments; the two mechanisms are different.
example:
#include <xc.inc>

ITEM_COUNT EQU 5
STEP_SIZE  EQU 2

PSECT equCode,class=CODE,reloc=2
load_count:
    MOVLW ITEM_COUNT      ; WREG = 5
    ADDLW STEP_SIZE       ; WREG = 7
    RETURN
; ITEM_COUNT and STEP_SIZE occupy no data-memory bytes.

name: #define
description: Defines a preprocessor macro: a name that is replaced by source text before the assembler sees it. A macro can also accept parameters.

operands.name: name
operands.description: Case-sensitive macro name.

operands.name: parameters
operands.description: Optional comma-separated names in parentheses immediately after the macro name; no intervening space.

operands.name: replacement
operands.description: Text to substitute; parenthesize expression parameters and the complete expression.

notes: Use a .S source filename (uppercase S), or the pic-as option -xassembler-with-cpp, to enable preprocessing. #define is a preprocessor directive, not an executable instruction.
It allocates no storage. Use EQU for an assembler constant or DS for a variable. End #define at the newline; use C-style comments on its line rather than an assembler semicolon comment.
example:
#include <xc.inc>

#define BASE_VALUE 0x20
#define NEXT_VALUE(x) ((x) + 1)

PSECT defineCode,class=CODE,reloc=2
load_next:
    MOVLW NEXT_VALUE(BASE_VALUE)
    ; After preprocessing: MOVLW ((0x20) + 1)
    ; Executing the instruction sets WREG to 0x21.
    RETURN

sources.title: PIC Assembler User's Guide: Preprocessor Directives

name: BANKSEL
short: Select the data bank for a variable
description: Generates the instructions needed to select the data-memory bank containing symbol. On PIC18 this selects the Bank Select Register (BSR) value used by banked file-register instructions.

operands.name: symbol
operands.description: Data-memory symbol or full address whose bank must be selected.

notes: BANKSEL selects a bank; the following file-register instruction must still use banked access (a=1) and the bank-relative address. BANKMASK removes the bank bits from a full address.
Access Bank instructions (a=0) do not use BSR. BANKSEL emits executable code; it is not just a naming or placement directive.
example:
#include <xc.inc>

PSECT udata_bank1
sample: DS 1

PSECT bankSelectCode,class=CODE,reloc=2
store_sample:
    BANKSEL sample         ; PIC18: select bank 1 in BSR
    MOVLW 0x2A
    MOVWF BANKMASK(sample),1 ; sample = 0x2A using banked access
    RETURN

name: CONFIG
description: Specifies configuration bits programmed into the device, such as oscillator mode, watchdog operation, and programming options. These settings are part of the programmed image, not instructions executed in sequence.

operands.name: setting
operands.description: Device-specific configuration setting, or a configuration register name.

operands.name: value
operands.description: Named setting value; a register form takes a numeric literal.

notes: The example targets PIC18F4520. Names and available values depend on the selected device; check its configuration documentation.
ON and OFF are named choices, not a guarantee that the underlying bit value is 1 or 0. The oscillator setting must match the hardware.
example:
#include <xc.inc>

; PIC18F4520 configuration choices:
CONFIG OSC = INTIO67       ; internal oscillator; RA6/RA7 are port pins
CONFIG WDT = OFF           ; watchdog disabled by configuration
CONFIG LVP = OFF           ; low-voltage programming disabled
CONFIG XINST = OFF         ; standard instruction set

PSECT configCode,class=CODE,reloc=2
idle:
    BRA idle
; CONFIG does not execute when the processor reaches this code.

name: ORG
short: Set the position within a section
description: Moves the current section position forward to the specified offset from that section's base. In an abs,ovrld section, the base is zero, so the offset is an absolute address.

operands.name: offset
operands.description: Absolute value or expression referring to the current section; cannot move the current position backward.

notes: ORG alone does not fix the final address of a relocatable section. To place one at an absolute address, use a separate section and the linker placement option.
ORG skips positions; it does not itself emit instructions or initialize every skipped byte.
example:
#include <xc.inc>

PSECT fixedTable,class=CONST,abs,ovrld
ORG 0x100
first_byte:
    DB 0x11                ; program address 0x100
ORG 0x104
second_byte:
    DB 0x22                ; program address 0x104

examples.title: Offset in a relocatable section
examples.code:
#include <xc.inc>

PSECT offsetData,class=CONST
ORG 0x10
value_byte:
    DB 0x33
; If linked with -Wl,-PoffsetData=0x200,
; value_byte is at 0x210, not 0x10.

name: ALIGN
short: Align the next item within a section
description: Advances the position within the current section to the requested byte boundary. It can align the next object or make the section length a multiple of a boundary.

operands.name: boundary
operands.description: Alignment boundary in bytes, for example 2 or 4.

notes: Alignment is relative to the section base. Give the section a matching reloc alignment if the final absolute address must also be aligned.
example:
#include <xc.inc>

PSECT alignedData,class=CONST,reloc=4
first_byte:
    DB 0x11
ALIGN 4
next_byte:
    DB 0x22
; next_byte is 4 bytes after first_byte.
; reloc=4 also aligns the section base to a multiple of 4.

name: GLOBAL
description: Makes symbols defined in this source module visible to other modules. For a symbol not defined here, GLOBAL instead declares a reference to a public symbol defined elsewhere.

operands.name: symbol
operands.description: Label or other symbol to export, or reference from another module.

notes: GLOBAL exports symbols; the PSECT global attribute controls section combination and does not export labels.
Save the examples as provider.S and caller.S and link both files. GLOBAL itself emits no executable code.
example:
; Save as provider.S
#include <xc.inc>
GLOBAL load_value

PSECT providerCode,class=CODE,reloc=2
load_value:
    MOVLW 0x2A
    RETURN

examples.title: caller.S
examples.code:
; Save as caller.S
#include <xc.inc>
EXTRN load_value
GLOBAL caller

PSECT callerCode,class=CODE,reloc=2
caller:
    CALL load_value        ; linker resolves the other file's label
    RETURN                 ; WREG is 0x2A after the call
; Assemble and link caller.S and provider.S together.

name: EXTRN
short: Reference symbols defined in another module
description: Declares a reference to a public symbol defined in another source module. The linker resolves its address when the modules are linked.

operands.name: symbol
operands.description: External symbol exported by the defining module with GLOBAL.

notes: The spelling in pic-as is EXTRN. Defining the same symbol in this module is an error.
Save the examples as caller.S and provider.S and link both files; assembling only caller.S does not provide the missing definition.
example:
; Save as caller.S
#include <xc.inc>
EXTRN load_value
GLOBAL caller

PSECT callerCode,class=CODE,reloc=2
caller:
    CALL load_value        ; linker resolves the other file's label
    RETURN                 ; WREG is 0x2A after the call
; Assemble and link caller.S and provider.S together.

examples.title: provider.S
examples.code:
; Save as provider.S
#include <xc.inc>
GLOBAL load_value

PSECT providerCode,class=CODE,reloc=2
load_value:
    MOVLW 0x2A
    RETURN

name: INCLUDE
description: Reads the named file as assembly source at this location. Included definitions are available to the assembler as if they appeared here.

operands.name: filename
operands.description: Assembly include file; use an appropriate path when it is outside the working directory.

notes: INCLUDE runs in the assembler. #include runs earlier in the preprocessor; preprocessing directives in a file read only by INCLUDE will not go back through the preprocessor.
Save the second example as options.inc beside the first and assemble from that directory.
example:
#include <xc.inc>
INCLUDE "options.inc"

PSECT includeCode,class=CODE,reloc=2
load_option:
    MOVLW OPTION_VALUE     ; WREG = 0x2A
    RETURN

examples.title: options.inc
examples.code:
; Assembly definitions included by INCLUDE:
OPTION_VALUE EQU 0x2A

name: MACRO
short: Define a reusable block of assembly
description: Defines a named template ending at ENDM. Invoking its name inserts a copy of the body with the supplied arguments substituted for the parameters.

operands.name: name
operands.description: Macro name, placed before MACRO.

operands.name: parameter,...
operands.description: Optional comma-separated parameter names; supply matching arguments when invoking the macro.

notes: Each invocation emits a new copy of the body; it is not a subroutine call. Use LOCAL for labels inside a macro that can be expanded more than once.
Use #define for preprocessing text substitution. MACRO is expanded later by the assembler.
example:
#include <xc.inc>

STORE_BYTE MACRO destination,literal
    MOVLW literal
    MOVWF destination,0
ENDM

PSECT macroCode,class=CODE,reloc=2
store_pair:
    STORE_BYTE 0x20,0x2A  ; expands to MOVLW + MOVWF
    STORE_BYTE 0x21,0x55  ; a second copy with other operands
    RETURN
; After execution: f[0x20] = 0x2A, f[0x21] = 0x55.

name: ENDM
short: End a macro or repetition block
description: Terminates the body of MACRO or REPT. It marks the end of an assembly-time block and does not generate a processor return instruction.
notes: ENDM pairs with MACRO or REPT. RETURN is a separate executable instruction used to return from a subroutine.
example:
#include <xc.inc>

STORE_BYTE MACRO destination,literal
    MOVLW literal
    MOVWF destination,0
ENDM

PSECT macroCode,class=CODE,reloc=2
store_pair:
    STORE_BYTE 0x20,0x2A  ; expands to MOVLW + MOVWF
    STORE_BYTE 0x21,0x55  ; a second copy with other operands
    RETURN
; After execution: f[0x20] = 0x2A, f[0x21] = 0x55.

name: LOCAL
short: Give each macro expansion unique labels
description: Within a macro, declares symbols that receive distinct assembler-generated names for each expansion. This allows the same macro body to define a label more than once without a duplicate definition.

operands.name: symbol
operands.description: Macro-internal label or symbol that must be unique per expansion.

notes: LOCAL is an assembler directive for macro symbols. The PSECT local attribute instead separates same-name sections from different modules.
example:
#include <xc.inc>

COUNT_DOWN MACRO destination
    LOCAL again
    MOVLW 2
    MOVWF destination,0
again:
    DECFSZ destination,1,0
    BRA again
ENDM

PSECT localCode,class=CODE,reloc=2
clear_pair:
    COUNT_DOWN 0x20        ; unique instance of again
    COUNT_DOWN 0x21        ; another instance; no duplicate label
    RETURN
; Each byte counts 2 -> 1 -> 0.

name: REPT
description: Expands the block up to ENDM the specified number of times while assembling. The resulting program contains that many copies of its instructions or data.

operands.name: count
operands.description: Number of block expansions; provide an assembly-time constant.

notes: REPT does not generate a runtime loop or a loop counter. Use a branch instruction when repetition must be controlled during execution.
example:
#include <xc.inc>

PSECT repeatCode,class=CODE,reloc=2
add_three:
    MOVLW 0
    REPT 3
        ADDLW 1
    ENDM
    RETURN
; The output contains three ADDLW 1 instructions.
; Executing them changes WREG: 0 -> 1 -> 2 -> 3.

name: SET
short: Define or redefine an assembler value
description: Associates a symbol with a value during assembly and permits a later SET to change it. Unlike a variable, the symbol has no reserved storage or runtime value to update.

operands.name: symbol
operands.description: Assembler symbol, placed before SET.

operands.name: expression
operands.description: Expression whose value is assigned at this point during assembly.

notes: EQU requires a new symbol; SET allows redefinition. DS reserves storage when a runtime variable is needed.
example:
#include <xc.inc>

STEP_VALUE SET 1
PSECT setCode,class=CODE,reloc=2
add_values:
    MOVLW STEP_VALUE      ; assembled as MOVLW 1
STEP_VALUE SET 2
    ADDLW STEP_VALUE      ; assembled as ADDLW 2
    RETURN                ; WREG = 3
; SET itself creates no instruction and changes no data-memory byte.

name: IF
description: Starts an assembly-time conditional block. A nonzero constant expression selects the following instructions for output; zero selects a later matching branch.

operands.name: expression
operands.description: Assembly-time constant expression; zero is false and nonzero is true.

notes: Conditions are evaluated during assembly, not during execution. Use processor tests and branches for runtime decisions.
The assembler still processes directives such as EQU in either branch. Define symbols outside this block; use preprocessor #if when whole source lines must be excluded before assembly.
Assembler equality uses = (or eq); preprocessor #if uses ==. ELSIF has no E after the S.
example:
#include <xc.inc>
MODE_VALUE EQU 2

PSECT conditionalCode,class=CODE,reloc=2
load_mode:
    IF MODE_VALUE = 2
        MOVLW 0x22        ; only this MOVLW is emitted
    ELSE
        MOVLW 0x33
    ENDIF
    RETURN
; Executing the selected code puts 0x22 in WREG.

name: ELSIF
description: Adds another condition to an IF block. Its instructions are emitted only when no preceding branch was selected and this condition is nonzero.

operands.name: expression
operands.description: Additional assembly-time constant expression.

notes: Conditions are evaluated during assembly, not during execution. Use processor tests and branches for runtime decisions.
The assembler still processes directives such as EQU in either branch. Define symbols outside this block; use preprocessor #if when whole source lines must be excluded before assembly.
Assembler equality uses = (or eq); preprocessor #if uses ==. ELSIF has no E after the S.
pic-as treats ELSIF as a nested ELSE + IF. Close the extra condition with another ENDIF, as shown in the guide's example and verified with XC8 v4.00.
example:
#include <xc.inc>
MODE_VALUE EQU 2

PSECT conditionalCode,class=CODE,reloc=2
load_mode:
    IF MODE_VALUE = 1
        MOVLW 0x11
    ELSIF MODE_VALUE = 2
        MOVLW 0x22        ; only this MOVLW is emitted
    ELSE
        MOVLW 0x33
    ENDIF                 ; close the IF introduced by ELSIF
    ENDIF                 ; close the original IF
    RETURN
; Executing the selected code puts 0x22 in WREG.

name: ELSE
description: Adds a fallback branch to an IF block. Its instructions are emitted when no preceding IF or ELSIF branch was selected.
notes: Conditions are evaluated during assembly, not during execution. Use processor tests and branches for runtime decisions.
The assembler still processes directives such as EQU in either branch. Define symbols outside this block; use preprocessor #if when whole source lines must be excluded before assembly.
Assembler equality uses = (or eq); preprocessor #if uses ==. ELSIF has no E after the S.
example:
#include <xc.inc>
MODE_VALUE EQU 2

PSECT conditionalCode,class=CODE,reloc=2
load_mode:
    IF MODE_VALUE = 2
        MOVLW 0x22        ; only this MOVLW is emitted
    ELSE
        MOVLW 0x33
    ENDIF
    RETURN
; Executing the selected code puts 0x22 in WREG.

name: ENDIF
description: Closes the matching IF block. Subsequent instructions are outside that conditional block.
notes: Conditions are evaluated during assembly, not during execution. Use processor tests and branches for runtime decisions.
The assembler still processes directives such as EQU in either branch. Define symbols outside this block; use preprocessor #if when whole source lines must be excluded before assembly.
Assembler equality uses = (or eq); preprocessor #if uses ==. ELSIF has no E after the S.
example:
#include <xc.inc>
MODE_VALUE EQU 2

PSECT conditionalCode,class=CODE,reloc=2
load_mode:
    IF MODE_VALUE = 2
        MOVLW 0x22        ; only this MOVLW is emitted
    ELSE
        MOVLW 0x33
    ENDIF
    RETURN
; Executing the selected code puts 0x22 in WREG.

name: END
description: Ends assembly of the source file. An optional expression records an entry point in the object file; whether the linker uses it depends on the build.

operands.name: entry_label
operands.description: Optional entry-point expression recorded in the object file.

notes: END is optional. If present, put it at the end of the source with nothing following.
END does not halt the processor and does not set the PIC18 reset vector. Use an executable loop for a running program that must remain in place, and place reset code separately.
example:
#include <xc.inc>

PSECT endCode,class=CODE,reloc=2
idle:
    BRA idle              ; executable loop keeps the processor here
END idle                  ; assembler source ends here

name: #include
description: Inserts a file during preprocessing. Both its preprocessor directives and its assembly contents are then available to the rest of the source.

operands.name: filename
operands.description: Use quotes for a project file, or angle brackets for a header such as <xc.inc>.

notes: Use a .S source filename (uppercase S), or -xassembler-with-cpp, to enable preprocessing.
Save the second example as project.inc beside the source. The include guard prevents repeated inclusion from defining its contents again.

sources.title: PIC Assembler User's Guide: Preprocessor Directives

name: #if
short: Select source by a preprocessing condition
description: Before assembly, includes source lines when the preprocessor expression is nonzero and excludes them when it is zero.

operands.name: expression
operands.description: Preprocessor expression using macros such as those defined with #define. Equality uses ==.

notes: Use a .S source filename (uppercase S), or -xassembler-with-cpp, to enable preprocessing.
Preprocessing happens before assembler symbols such as EQU are evaluated. Use #define for these conditions, or use assembler IF to test assembler constants.
example:
#include <xc.inc>
#define MODE_VALUE 2

PSECT preConditionalCode,class=CODE,reloc=2
load_mode:
#if MODE_VALUE == 1
    MOVLW 0x11
#elif MODE_VALUE == 2
    MOVLW 0x22            ; only this source branch reaches assembly
#else
    MOVLW 0x33
#endif
    RETURN                ; WREG = 0x22

name: #ifdef
short: Include source if a macro exists
description: Includes source lines when the named preprocessor macro is defined. It tests existence, not the numeric value of its replacement text.

operands.name: name
operands.description: Preprocessor macro name, without parentheses.

notes: Use a .S source filename (uppercase S), or -xassembler-with-cpp, to enable preprocessing.
A macro defined as 0 still satisfies #ifdef. Use #if when the replacement value should be tested.
example:
#include <xc.inc>
#define FEATURE_VALUE 0

PSECT ifdefCode,class=CODE,reloc=2
load_feature:
#ifdef FEATURE_VALUE
    MOVLW 0x2A            ; selected: FEATURE_VALUE exists, even as 0
#else
    MOVLW 0x00
#endif
    RETURN

name: #ifndef
short: Include source if a macro is absent
description: Includes source lines when the named preprocessor macro is not defined. Useful for default values and include guards that prevent repeated definitions.

operands.name: name
operands.description: Preprocessor macro name whose absence should be tested.

notes: Use a .S source filename (uppercase S), or -xassembler-with-cpp, to enable preprocessing.
A default guarded with #ifndef preserves a definition already supplied by the project or the command line.
example:
#include <xc.inc>
#ifndef BUFFER_SIZE
#define BUFFER_SIZE 4
#endif

PSECT ifndefCode,class=CODE,reloc=2
load_buffer_size:
    MOVLW BUFFER_SIZE     ; WREG = 4 when no override is provided
    RETURN
; Building with -DBUFFER_SIZE=8 instead emits MOVLW 8.

name: #undef
description: Removes the definition of the named macro for subsequent preprocessing. It emits no code and does not change symbols created by assembler EQU or SET.

operands.name: name
operands.description: Macro name to undefine.

notes: Use a .S source filename (uppercase S), or -xassembler-with-cpp, to enable preprocessing.
example:
#include <xc.inc>
#define FEATURE_VALUE 1
#undef FEATURE_VALUE

PSECT undefCode,class=CODE,reloc=2
load_without_feature:
#ifdef FEATURE_VALUE
    MOVLW 0x11
#else
    MOVLW 0x22            ; selected: the macro was removed
#endif
    RETURN
